Hybrid work across distributed operations demands security that follows users and traffic across remote sites and cloud apps

Connects securely across offices, field locations, remote workers, and hybrid cloud resources under consistent policy

Replaces fragmented tools with unified policy and visibility, reducing admin effort and speeding issue resolution
Keeps users and applications securely connected across campus, remote, and cloud environments, minimizing downtime
Helps agencies meet zero trust mandates through consistent access control and enforcement, reducing audit and remediation risk

Policy where the network lives: Identity, device context, segmentation, and enforcement connected across the infrastructure itself, not bolted on as a separate security overlay
Security paired with sight: End-to-end application, network, internet, and user-experience visibility alongside protection, not protection without the ability to see or troubleshoot
Compliance built in, not bolted on: Capabilities aligned to FedRAMP, FIPS, and DoD requirements designed for government from the ground up, not federal compliance retrofitted after the fact
One architecture, edge to cloud: A common platform spanning access, branch, WAN, data center, and cloud, not a patchwork of point solutions at every layer

overview.description: Critical infrastructure and operational environments must stay safe, available, and resilient against cyber and operational disruption. content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: Threat actors increasingly perceiving ICS vulnerabilities
Automation in ICS increasing attack vectors and surfaces
Evolution to software-defined service updates and delivery
Availability of sophisticated hacking tools increasing the pool of capable attackers
Capabilities driven by AI/ML enhancing ICS operations and security

content.title: Capabilities

Continually evolve solutions and capabilities, with updates automatically delivered to client tools
Automatically update threat defenses via dynamic threat feeds
Deliver high resolution, unified visibility into network and application performance to prevent issues

businessOverview.description: Cisco unifies operational technology (OT) visibility, segmentation, and identity-based policy in one architecture—helping agencies protect critical infrastructure while simplifying operations and compliance. With Cisco Cyber Vision, Cisco Secure Firewall, and Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) working together under Cisco Industrial Threat Defense, agencies can secure industrial environments without stitching together disconnected point solutions.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Greater visibility into OT assets and communications closes blind spots, lowering risk and sharpening remediation priorities
Stronger segmentation, access control, and monitoring cut both the likelihood and impact of incidents, avoiding costly disruption to essential services
More secure, reliable industrial environments boost uptime and continuity for mission-critical operations like utilities, transportation, and facilities
Safer remote access reduces third-party and maintenance-related exposure while speeding support and boosting workforce efficiency
Stronger controls and auditability help agencies meet regulatory and critical-infrastructure requirements, cutting compliance risk and strengthening governance

content.title: Differentiators
content.subTitle: Why Cisco
list: Single architecture, not a patchwork: Switching, routing, visibility, segmentation, identity, remote access, and SOC integration unified under one vendor
One embedded fabric: OT asset visibility built into the industrial network itself, not separate sensors or overlay hardware
Security in the network, not on top of it: The industrial network enforces security directly, rather than security bolted on after connectivity
Context-driven segmentation: Enforcement based on real asset and communication context across industrial zones, not static policy alone
Connected detection and response: OT telemetry, threat intelligence, and incident response unified across IT and OT, not siloed tools

Detect and contain suspicious activity across endpoints, networks, and user accounts before it spreads into care delivery systems

Spot unusual behavior earlier and help teams focus on the highest-risk activity when time and staff are limited

overview.name: Hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure
overview.description: Healthcare organizations are under pressure to manage growing data volumes, support AI use cases, and modernize infrastructure without disrupting care. Hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure means running data, applications, and AI workloads across on-premises and cloud environments in a way that supports security, performance, and flexibility. This helps organizations use data more effectively, scale new capabilities faster, and support clinical and business workloads.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: Research organizations need support to accelerate trial timelines
Decentralized clinical trials gain ground, increasing participant enrollment diversity
High operational costs and dropout rates plague traditional trial formats, calling for reduction
Highly valuable intellectual property and sensitive participant health data require protection
Evolving global regulatory frameworks for trial data collection demand adherence

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Bridge on-premises data centers with multiple public cloud environments seamlessly
Deploy high-performance networking infrastructure capable of supporting AI workloads
Enforce consistent security and compliance policies across hybrid environments
Optimize cloud resource spending while maintaining peak application performance
Secure data transmission between edge devices, data centers, and cloud storage

successStories.description: See how other organizations have applied Cisco solutions.

businessOverview.description: Cisco helps healthcare organizations build hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure by connecting data center, networking, security, and observability technologies so workloads can run across on-premises and cloud environments with more consistency. In particular, Cisco helps tie these pieces together across the full environment — so organizations do not have to manage the gaps between multiple disconnected platforms.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Scale computational resources dynamically to handle spikes in data processing
Enable faster deployment of organizations' AI-driven clinical tools
Reduce capital expenditures by optimizing hybrid cloud asset utilization
Support organizations' regulatory-compliance efforts through data-residency controls
Support high availability for mission-critical EHR systems

content.title: Differentiators
content.subTitle: Why Cisco
list: End-to-end AI stack: Network, compute, security, observability, and hybrid-cloud operations covered as one, not a single layer patched to someone else's
Unified silicon: One architecture across access, core, and AI networks, so data moves consistently everywhere, not a fragmented portfolio bolted together
AI at the edge: Compute, networking, security, and storage converged where care happens, not stranded in a central data center
Security from network to workload: Identity, segmentation, and runtime protection tied together across the stack, not point protection in one domain
Observability built in: Full-stack telemetry correlated with the infrastructure it runs on, not a monitoring tool sitting off to the side

Care teams coordinate more effectively in service of patient-safety goals

Strict communication standards for protected health information require compliance

overview.name: Medical device integration
overview.description: Healthcare organizations are managing more connected devices than ever before while working to reduce clinician workload, close documentation gaps, and improve patient safety. This use case connects critical clinical devices and related systems so data flows automatically instead of relying on manual transcription, with AI helping surface insights and flag issues in real time. The result is better data accuracy, a more complete patient view, and less workflow burden for care teams.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: Connected medical and Internet of Things (IoT) devices rise in volume, expanding the attack surface
Demand for real-time, remote patient monitoring grows across inpatient and home settings
HIPAA and risk-management obligations require organizational support
Ransomware and cyber threats targeting healthcare networks escalate
Interoperability between devices and electronic medical record systems advances

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Connect devices securely and automatically to the electronic health record (EHR) and care systems
Segment networks to isolate medical devices from administrative and guest traffic
Gain full visibility into every device connecting to the network
Aggregate and route patient data securely to dashboards and records
Maintain uninterrupted connectivity for clinical workflows

businessOverview.description: Cisco helps integrate medical devices by combining the hospital network, secure wireless access, device visibility, segmentation, and AI-driven insights so devices connect reliably to care systems without creating unmanaged risk. Cisco’s advantage is that it does this across the full environment — from bedside connectivity to security and operational visibility — so organizations do not have to stitch together separate vendors to keep devices securely connected.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Help protect patient data and devices and reduce the risk of breaches and downtime
Enable organizations to route contextual data to clinicians who inform their own decisions
Help reduce risk exposure through automated threat detection and segmentation
Streamline integration between devices and medical record systems
Support organizations in strengthening compliance posture and audit readiness

content.title: Differentiators
content.subTitle: Why Cisco
list: Network-based enforcement: Securing medical devices through existing infrastructure, not standalone tools
Native infrastructure control: Combining device visibility with network-wide enforcement, not just passive identification
Policy-based segmentation: Tying device profiling directly to zero-trust enforcement, not just simple discovery
Agentless protection: Securing legacy devices that cannot support software agents, not relying on endpoint-dependent security
Unified zero trust: Integrating device security into the broader enterprise architecture, not treating it as a separate project

overview.name: Digital experiences and wayfinding
overview.description: Healthcare organizations need to make care easier to access while simplifying navigation across large and often confusing campuses. This use case consists of using mobile, location-based, and digital tools to help people navigate facilities, find services, and stay connected to the right information during their visit. This helps reduce stress, missed appointments, and delays while improving how patients and staff move through the care environment.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: Low patient satisfaction scores caused by frustrating hospital navigation call for improvement
Revenue losses from late or missed clinical appointments require reduction
Hospital brands stand out in competitive markets through digital consumer tools
Foot traffic flow needs optimization to prevent overcrowding in main corridors
Modern healthcare consumers demand mobile-first digital interactions

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Deploy high-density indoor wireless networks supporting hyper-accurate location tracking
Integrate location-based services with patient-facing mobile application software
Support user privacy through secure, anonymized location-data processing
Analyze visitor movement patterns to optimize hospital floor layouts
Provide seamless, automated guest Wi-Fi onboarding to enhance engagement

businessOverview.description: Cisco helps healthcare organizations support digital experiences and wayfinding by combining wireless infrastructure, location services, and analytics so patients and staff can navigate facilities more easily and access the right information at the right time. What sets Cisco apart is the ability to use the existing network as the foundation for both connectivity and location-based insight, giving health systems a more unified way to improve the care experience.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Help organizations reduce missed-appointment rates by guiding patients to clinics
Help organizations improve patient experience related to accessibility
Reduce front-desk staff interruptions by providing digital self-service navigation
Optimize facility space utilization using real-time visitor foot-traffic analytics
Drive deeper digital patient engagement with timely, location-aware notifications

content.title: Differentiators
content.subTitle: Why Cisco
list: One network: Cisco turns the hospital's existing network into the foundation for secure wayfinding, mobile engagement, and location intelligence, not a bolt-on system
Single architecture: Enterprise healthcare wireless, indoor location, secure onboarding, and zero-trust policy in a single design, not four separate tools
Broader payoff: A wayfinding project becomes a platform for patient flow, asset visibility, occupancy analytics, and staff mobility, not a single-purpose spend
Shared foundation: Mobile digital experiences run on the same observability and security layer that supports clinical operations, not a parallel stack
Unified fabric: Location intelligence, collaboration, and networking pulled together to lift both patient experience and hospital workflow, not unrelated projects

overview.name: Claims automation and anomaly detection
overview.description: Billing errors, duplicate claims, and unusual charges can create payment issues, extra manual work, and compliance risk for healthcare organizations. By flagging claims for review before payment, teams can improve accuracy, reduce rework, and focus attention on the claims that need it most.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: High claims volume and limited staff make manual review difficult to sustain
Billing errors, duplicate claims, and denials create avoidable rework and payment delays
Fraud, waste, and inappropriate billing require earlier detection before claims are paid
Audit, compliance, and documentation requirements increase pressure on claims operations
Tight margins and rising administrative costs make claims accuracy and efficiency more important

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Implement real-time data inspection across secure health network perimeters
Integrate high-performance computing resources to run predictive fraud algorithms
Enable automated workflows that help organizations surface patterns for their own review
Unify disparate billing systems into a secure, centralized data pipeline
Support continuous compliance logging to help organizations meet audit obligations

businessOverview.description: Cisco helps healthcare organizations support claims automation and anomaly detection across clinical, billing, and cloud environments with a more secure and reliable foundation. By combining Cisco’s AI-ready infrastructure, security, and Splunk-based visibility, teams can move data across systems more consistently, spot issues earlier, and reduce the operational gaps that slow claims review or increase risk.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Faster claims processing helps reduce payment delays and improve cash flow
Earlier detection of errors and anomalies helps prevent avoidable financial loss
Less manual review helps lower administrative burden on billing teams
Better claims accuracy helps reduce denials, rework, and missed revenue
More consistent review and documentation helps support compliance and audits

Better operational visibility: Splunk, ThousandEyes, and Cisco security tools help teams detect issues earlier across systems and networks
Flexible deployment: Cisco supports on-prem, cloud, and hybrid models based on how the organization operates
Broader platform support: Cisco can help connect, secure, monitor, and support the environment around the use case, not just one part of it

By combining reliable high-speed connectivity, simple device onboarding, secure access, location-aware services, and smarter residence hall operations, you create a seamless, home-like living experience that improves student satisfaction, engagement, and retention.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: High student expectations, driven by high tuition rates, must be met
The home wireless experience students expect requires delivery
Residential wireless apps that monitor student engagement and success call for support
Plug-and-play access serves many student devices on campus networks
Private living residences present competition to meet

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Ease the transition for students from home to university life
Retain students in residence hall contracts to increase revenue
Provide advantages over private residences
Reduce the complexity of residence hall network operational support
Address increasing wireless bandwidth demand from students

content.title: Benefits

overview.name: Research and academic computing
overview.description: Build scalable, interconnected high-performance computing (HPC) and AI/ML infrastructure that powers groundbreaking research across disciplines. Support simulation, data analytics, and large-scale scientific workloads through shared graphics processing unit (GPU) clusters and federated platforms that universities and research institutions can access collaboratively.

content.title: Industry drivers
content.subTitle: What makes this important
list: Explosive AI/ML research growth demands GPU-intensive compute
High-throughput analysis of rising scientific data volumes requires enablement
Demand for federated, cross-institution research collaboration increases and must be met
Costly compute resources across departments call for optimization
Sensitive research data requires secure handling

content.title: Capabilities
content.subTitle: What this enables you to do
list: Scale high performance computing and AI/ML compute to grow with research demand
Deliver high-performance, low-latency interconnect across clusters
Provide shared, multi-tenant access to GPU and compute resources
Secure data movement and storage for sensitive workloads
Simplify management of complex, distributed infrastructure

businessOverview.description: Cisco delivers the high-performance, AI-ready infrastructure and secure networking that let institutions run demanding computational workloads at scale while keeping research data protected and accessible across campuses and partner sites.

content.title: Benefits
content.subTitle: How is the business value generated
list: Deliver high-speed networking fabric that connects HPC and AI/ML clusters efficiently
Enable secure, segmented access to shared research platforms
Reduce operational complexity through unified infrastructure management
Support elastic scaling to handle peak research and simulation loads
Strengthen data protection across federated, multi-institution environments

content.title: Differentiators
content.subTitle: Why Cisco
list: One architecture: Compute, networking, security, and observability connected end to end, so research clusters, AI workloads, and shared campus IT run as one system
Campus to AI fabric: A unified architecture across access, core, data center, and AI networking, giving institutions consistency, scale, and performance in mixed environments
AI-ready by design: Pre-validated, modular, scalable infrastructure with security and operations built in, so AI-intensive research starts from proven designs
Security built in: Protection woven through networking, firewalling, analytics, detection, and infrastructure design, so IP, regulated data, and shared compute are covered from the start
Simplicity at scale: Lifecycle, telemetry, and management brought together to cut complexity, not just add hardware
